AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Burn patients are an especially high-risk population for development of central line associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) due to open wounds, extended length of intensive care unit stay, frequent use of central venous catheters, and generally immunocompromised state. Implementing evidence-based practices to prevent these infections is a 2014 National Patient Safety Goal per The Joint Commission.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this project was introduction of a commercially available alcohol impregnated central venous line port protector to reduce the incidence of CLABSI in the burn unit.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The Iowa Model for Implementing Evidenced-Based Practice was used to guide this intervention conducted by the Unit Practice Council. A pre- and post-intervention design compared rates of CLABSI before and after introduction of the port protectors.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: CLABSI infection rates decreased following the intervention from baseline of 7.3 per 1000 line days to an average of 3.04 per 1000 line days during calendar year 2013.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Introduction of an alcohol impregnated central venous line port protector can reduce the incidence of CLABSI in a burn unit.
